posts.reason: A Thoughtworks lead reports a week-long experiment with no human-written code, and the thread tests her accountability argument against pair programming and TDD.
Dan Luu backs a contrarian case with his own quick builds and the pgrust rewrite, and the thread answers with concrete reports of fragile AI-written code.
Twelve years of first-hand history reduced to a clear framework: consensus, streaming and merge, with the projects that took each path.
A short post with one stylesheet, but the thread digs into whether sites should set font sizes at all and how code reads on paper.
A sourced history from 1860 to 1968 showing how slowly building codes move, and how the answer recommended in 1881 took decades to win.
Five concrete tactics for earning influence without seniority, from someone who hires, with anecdotes from Stripe, Notion and Anthropic.
A worked reverse-engineering session with an AI agent, Ghidra and live memory reads, with code excerpts for rendering and scoring.
One engineer's contribution data from 2019 to 2026 shows cheap implementation pulling in more work, and the thread trades ways to push back.
The chart is a single number; the value is in long first-hand accounts from former heavy answerers on why they stopped.
A monastery explains its CNC workflow for Gothic stone, and the thread weighs machine roughing against hand finishing, with Sagrada Familia as a case.
One of the largest proofs in mathematics checked by Lean's kernel, with project engineers answering how incompatible definitions get reconciled.
